assays.assay_description: HTR measured via custom-built magnetometer apparatus with magnetic ear tags. Mice placed in plastic containers (11.6 cm diameter x 13.3 cm height) surrounded by a coil. Recorded for 30 min after 5-HTP or 20 min after psilocybin, with dose-response and receptor modulator (M100907, 8-OH-DPAT, RS-102221, EPPTB) pretreatments.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection immediately before placing the weighed animals into the magnetometer.

time_to_assay.evidence: Drugs were administered by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection immediately before placing the weighed animals into the magnetometer.

outcomes.summary: 5-HTP (50-250 mg/kg) and psilocybin (0.1-25.6 mg/kg) induced dose-dependent increases in HTR; psilocybin showed a bimodal time profile. M100907 (5-HT2A antagonist) and 8-OH-DPAT (5-HT1A agonist) blocked HTR induced by both compounds. RS-102221 (5-HT2C antagonist) enhanced HTR at lower doses and reduced it at higher doses (inverted-U). EPPTB (TAAR1 antagonist) reduced 5-HTP-induced HTR but not psilocybin-induced HTR.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way repeated measures ANOVA: significant main effects of dose and time, and time x dose interactions. Detailed results in Supplementary Table S1.
outcomes.evidence: 5-HTP and psilocybin induced a dose-dependent increase in the frequency of HTR over 20 min with attenuation by the 5-HT2AR antagonist, M100907, and the 5-HT1AR agonist, 8-OH-DPAT.

judge_notes: Both candidates converged on a single HTR assay; merged into one entry.
